problems.question: A hydrocarbon has four carbons in a chain with one carbon–carbon double bond and no ring. How many hydrogen atoms does it hold?
problems.explanation: A chain of four carbons with single bonds holds 2 × 4 + 2 = 10 hydrogens. A double bond uses one more bond on each of two carbons, so two hydrogens fewer: 8.

problems.question: Hydrogen chloride, H–Cl, adds to ethene. Which pair of electrons moves first, and where does it go?

options.label: The second pair of the double bond moves to the hydrogen of H–Cl
The second pair of the double bond moves to the chlorine
A lone pair on chlorine moves to a carbon of ethene
A pair of a C–H bond moves to the hydrogen of H–Cl

problems.explanation: Chlorine attracts the pair it shares with hydrogen, so hydrogen is the electron-poor end of H–Cl. The double bond's second pair is the electron-rich site, and it moves to that hydrogen.
